# Darash

> The all-in-one research crate: async web search, page fetch, and HTML extraction in one Rust dependency. No API keys.

Darash (crates.io: `darash`, repo: https://github.com/tschk/darash) implements the research loop for agents:

- **Search**: `SearchClient::local()` runs an in-process multi-source backend by default; `SearchClient::new(endpoint)` targets any SearxNG-compatible endpoint. `SearchRequest` carries a Vane-compatible mode (speed/balanced/quality) and sources (web/academic/discussions); responses project into citations without an AI provider.
- **Fetch**: `darash::fetch::fetch(url, headers)` (a thin wrapper over `fetch_with(url, FetchOptions)`) returns a `FetchReport` with status, final URL, redirected flag, elapsed ms, content type, size, and body. Never silent, even on error statuses; bodies capped at 2 MiB (`FetchOptions::max_bytes` overrides). Options cover method, request body, basic auth, insecure TLS, and timeout. `fetch::read_source(path)` does the same for local files. `fetch::locate(html, text)` returns the deepest elements holding the text as CSS selector paths with snippets; `fetch::paginate(total, offset, limit)` returns `PageMeta` (`more`/`complete`/`past_end`).
- **Extract**: `to_markdown`, `to_text`, `outline` (repeating structures), `select_texts`, `rows(html, container, "title=h2, url=a@href")`, `tables` — all local and deterministic. `estimate_tokens` (≈4 chars/token) and `apply_budget` cut output at item boundaries within a token budget, always keeping at least one item. The `filter` module compiles the safe `--where` expression language; `disk_cache` is the CLI's short-lived on-disk body cache.

CLI (ships with the crate, `cargo install darash`):

- `darash search <query> [--mode speed|balanced|quality] [--source web|academic|discussions] [--url endpoint] [--json]`
- `darash fetch <url|file> [--md|--text|--outline|--select CSS [--count]|--row name=sel,url=a@href|--table|--locate TEXT|--body] [--limit N] [--offset N] [--where EXPR] [--budget N] [--json|--json-envelope]`
- Request flags: `-X/--method M`, `-d/--data BODY|@FILE|@-` (`@file`/`@-` strip CR/LF), `--data-raw B` (never reads `@` as a file), `--data-binary B` (keeps bytes), `-u USER:PASS`, `-I/--head`, `-k/--insecure`, `-m/--max-time SECS`, `--max-bytes N`, `--header 'Name: value'`, `-o FILE` (atomic write), `-f/--fail` (HTTP error → exit 22, report still printed), and the accepted no-ops `-L`, `-i`, `-s`, `-S`.
- Cache: fetched URL bodies are cached ~2 min under the user cache dir and reused by parse modes; bypassed by custom headers, non-`GET` methods, request bodies, `Cache-Control: no-store`, and credential-bearing URLs; `--fresh` refetches and re-caches, `--no-cache` never reads or writes. Hits announce their age on stderr.
- Fetch prints the full report as JSON by default (including the body); `--body` prints only the body; extraction modes print data on stdout and a one-line report plus omission/pagination notes on stderr. Rows and single tables default to TSV, `--json` switches them to JSON rows, and multiple tables always print JSON. `--json` wraps any mode as `{"data": …, "meta": {status, ok, url, ms, bytes, count, omitted}}`; `--json-envelope` prints `{"data": …, "meta": {state, total, offset, returned, next_offset}}`.

Hosted API: https://darash.tsc.hk exposes the same search + fetch loop over HTTP — `GET /api/health`, `GET /api/search?q=&mode=&limit=`, `GET /api/fetch?url=&md=1&select=&limit=`, and `GET /api/stats`.

Limits: 15 s search timeout (configurable via `SearchConfig::with_timeout`), 256 KiB search response cap, 2 MiB fetch body cap (override with `--max-bytes`), queries ≤ 512 chars, http/https only, no embedded credentials.
